headline: Cloudflare launches self-managed OAuth for all developers
summary: This new feature allows developers to easily create and manage their own OAuth clients for delegated access to the Cloudflare API, moving beyond less secure API tokens.
details: Cloudflare, powering 20% of the web, has rolled out self-managed OAuth, making it simpler for customers to create and manage their own OAuth clients. This enables delegated access to the Cloudflare API, crucial for developers building automations and integrations.

Previously, third-party OAuth was restricted to a few partners, forcing other developers to use API tokens. These tokens are harder to manage and less suitable for many delegated application flows, limiting broader integration capabilities.

With self-managed OAuth, developers can now offer a standard OAuth flow where users grant scoped access directly. This facilitates building SaaS integrations, internal developer platforms, and agentic tools with clearer consent and easier revocation.

Cloudflare also enhanced its consent experience, making application access requests and permissions clearer. Dashboard revocation and visible app ownership were added to prevent OAuth phishing attacks and improve user control.

Opening up OAuth to all customers necessitated significant upgrades to Cloudflare's underlying OAuth engine, Hydra. This involved extensive planning to ensure minimal user interruption and maintain data stability and security during the transition.

The upgrade process included two sequential updates, starting with a move to Hydra 1.X. Cloudflare rewrote SQL migrations to use features like CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and created a custom Hydra version to avoid schema migration issues and user impact.
